questions.question: A merchant marked his goods 20% above the cost price and sold the goods at a profit of 8%. The rate of discount is:

Profit % = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100

Profit = SP - CP

Selling price = [1 - Discount% / 100] x MP

Solution:

Profit = 0.08CP

Selling price = 0.08CP + CP = 1.08CP

M.P = C.P + 0.2 C.P = 1.2 CP

Now, let's find Dicount%,

1.08CP = [1 - Discount%/100] x 1.2CP

Discount% = 100 - 90 = 10%

Hence, the discount = 10%.

questions.question: The radius of a circle is increased by 20%. Find the percentage increase in the circumference of the circle.
questions.solution:
Given:

Increased radius = 120% of the Original radius

Formula used:

Circumference of circle = 2πr

Calculation:

Let the original radius be 5r.

Increased radius = 120% of Original radius

⇒ R = 120/100 × 5r

⇒ R = 6/5 × 5 = 6r

Original circumference = 2π(5r)

Increased circumference = 2π(6r)

Increased circumference = 2πr

Required percentage = (Increased circumference – Original circumference)/Original circumference × 100

= 2πr/2π(5r) × 100

⇒ 20%

**The percentage increase in the circumference of the circle is 20%.**

questions.question: A man borrowed a certain sum of money at the rate of 10% per annum simple interest for the first three years and 15% per annum simple interest for the period beyond three years. If he pays a total interest of Rs. 2884.50 at the end of 7 years, then the sum of money (in Rs.) that he borrowed is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Interest % = (Rate₁ × Time₁) + (Rate₂ × Time₂)

Total Interest % = (10% × 3) + (15% × (7 − 3)) = 30% + 60% = 90%

Given: 90% of Sum = ₹2884.50

Sum (100%) = (2884.50 ÷ 90) × 100 = 32.05 × 100 = ₹3205

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3205.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First rate (R₁) = 10%, Time (T₁) = 3 years

Second rate (R₂) = 15%, Time (T₂) = 7 − 3 = 4 years

Total Interest = ₹2884.50

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• Start 3 yrs 7 yrs 10% p.a. 15% p.a. Interest₁ = 30% of P Interest₂ = 60% of P Total Interest (90%) = ₹2884.50

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the borrowed sum be P.

⇒ SI for first 3 years = (P × 10 × 3) ÷ 100 = 30P ÷ 100

⇒ SI for next 4 years = (P × 15 × 4) ÷ 100 = 60P ÷ 100

⇒ Total SI = (30P ÷ 100) + (60P ÷ 100) = 90P ÷ 100

⇒ 90P ÷ 100 = 2884.50

⇒ 0.9P = 2884.50

⇒ P = 2884.50 ÷ 0.9

⇒ P = 28845 ÷ 9 = 3205

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3205.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Variable Rate Simple Interest

When interest rates change over time, the total interest is the sum of interest for each period: Total SI = P × (R₁T₁ + R₂T₂ + R₃T₃ + ...) ÷ 100.

Principal and Amount Relationship

The total amount (A) is the sum of the Principal (P) and the Total Simple Interest (SI): A = P + SI.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount, whereas compound interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods.

questions.question: A can finish a work in 25 days, and B can do the same work in 15 days. B worked for 10 days and left the job. A alone can finish the remaining work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(25, 15) = 75 units.

Efficiency of A = 75 ÷ 25 = 3 units/day; Efficiency of B = 75 ÷ 15 = 5 units/day.

Work completed by B in 10 days = 10 × 5 = 50 units.

Remaining work = 75 − 50 = 25 units.

Time taken by A = 25 ÷ 3 = 8 1/3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 1/3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 25 days

Time taken by B = 15 days

B leaves after working for 10 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A

 B

 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Work = LCM of 25 and 15 = 75 units

⇒ Work done by B in 10 days = 10 × 5 = 50 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 75 − 50 = 25 units

⇒ Time taken by A to finish the remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time = 25 ÷ 3 = 8 1/3 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 1/3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Works on the same principle as time and work, where inlet pipes perform positive work and outlet pipes (leaks) perform negative work.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual (Efficiency × Time), not just their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the combined work in one cycle (e.g., 2 days) and then find the total cycles required.</p

questions.question: The speed of a car going from A to B is 110 km/h, while coming back, its speed is 76 km/h. What is the average speed during the entire journey?
questions.solution:
Given:

The speed of a car going from A to B = 110 km/h

The speed of a car going from B to A = 76 km/h

Concept:

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

Calculation:

Let, the distance between A and B = x km

Time taken to go from A to B = x/110 hours

Time taken to go from B to A = x/76 hours

Total time = (x/110 + x/76)

Total distance covered = 2x km

His average speed = 2x/(x/110 + x/76)" id="MathJax-Element-16-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">" id="MathJax-Element-15-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0"> 

⇒ 2x/(186x/110 × 76)

⇒ (110 × 76)/93

⇒ 89(83/93) km/hr

∴ The car's average speed is** ****89(83/93) km**/hr.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** 

Average speed = 2 × (a × b)\(a + b)

where a and b are the two speeds to cover the same distance.

⇒ 2 × (110 × 76)\(110 + 76) 

⇒ (110 × 76)/93

⇒ 89(83/93)

questions.question: What is the third proportional of 2√3 and 6√5?

The third proportional proportion is the second term of the mean terms.

For example, if we have a ∶ b = c ∶ d, then the term ‘c’ is the third proportional to ‘a’ and ‘b’.

Represented as:

a : b ∷ b : c

Calculation:

Let the third proportion to 2√3 and 6√5 be x

⇒ 2√3/6√5 = 6√5/x

⇒ x = (6√5 × 6√5)/2√3

⇒ x = 90/√3

= 30√3

∴ The third proportional to **2√3 and 6√5**** is ****30√3.**

questions.question: The marked price on a fancy item is Rs. 250 but there is an 18% discount during festival season. The price of the fancy item after discount is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The marked price of a fancy item = Rs. 250

Discount = 18%.

Formula:

S.P = M.P × (100 - D%)/100

Where,

S.P = Selling price

M.P = Marked price

D = Discount%

Calculation:

S.P = M.P × (100 - D%)/100

⇒ 250 × (100 - 18)/100

⇒ 250 × 0.82 = 205

∴ The selling price of a **fancy item** is Rs. 205.
